title: China's Spiciest Pot Was Born on the Docks — Chongqing Hotpot · 九宫格 | China Travel Expert
description:
China's spiciest pot was born on the docks — not in a palace.

Chongqing hotpot traces back to boatmen and dock workers at the city's wharves in the late Ming / early Qing era. Cheap offal, beef tallow, chilies and Sichuan pepper went into one bubbling iron pot. To let strangers share it, cooks divided the pot into squares — the famous 九宫格 (nine-grid), one square per diner. Its soul is málà (麻辣): Sichuan peppercorn that numbs, chili that burns.

🧭 Expert Tip: New to málà? Order a 鸳鸯 (twin) pot — mild broth on one side, the fiery red on the other.

中国最辣的锅，生在重庆码头——九宫格火锅。
